summary: Osborne Lookout: BIA-designed ground-house lookout on Archuleta Mesa, Jicarilla Reservation; built 1959-60, registered 1999, listed standing; no later history found.

facts.design: Ground-level house with cupola, designed by the Bureau of Indian Affairs (register)

access.note: On the Jicarilla Reservation and administered by the BIA. I found no public visiting rules.

events.note: Register's Built field gives 1960; completed and staffed that year
Fires burned over 1,000 acres on and near the reservation that year; the register says the lookout played an important role

evidence.supports: Located on Archuleta Mesa, Jicarilla Reservation, Rio Arriba County
Located in Rio Arriba County, New Mexico
Construction begun in late summer 1959; fourth lookout on the Jicarilla Reservation
evidence.quote: During the late summer of 1959 construction was begun on Osborne Lookout, the fourth on the Jicarilla Reservation.

evidence.supports: Ground-level house with cupola designed by the BIA
evidence.quote: Located on Archuleta Mesa, the unique ground house with cupola was designed by the Bureau of Indian Affairs.

evidence.supports: Completed and staffed in 1960; fires burned over 1,000 acres that year
evidence.quote: Completed and staffed in 1960, the new lookout had an important role that year as fires burned over 1,000 acres on and near the reservation.

evidence.supports: Administered by the Bureau of Indian Affairs
evidence.quote: Administered by Bureau of Indian Affairs

evidence.supports: FFLA lists Osborn (Arachal) as a standing ground structure
evidence.quote: Osborn (Arachal) Rio Arriba 36.98353 -106.97072 Ground Standing NHLR US 318, NM 6

notes_for_editor: Thin: the register page is the only history source found, and the FFLA list supplies the standing status. Nothing found on the lookout after 1960 except its registration in 1999 and the standing listing. Searches for tribal or BIA records returned nothing usable. Archuleta Mesa attracts unreliable online material (some tying it to unrelated claims); none is used. The record's other_names 'Osborn (Arachal)' is confirmed by the FFLA list. The record's material 'wood' (material_from 'design') does not appear in the register text read, so it is not supported here; a human should check it. The register does not explain the name Osborne. Do not confuse it with the Osborne firefinder described in Zinn's Santa Fe history, which is an instrument and not this lookout.
